from.place: Proof, first paragraph: normalization is surjective and is an isomorphism over the dense normal locus; second paragraph: after an algebraically closed extension it is the normalization of the base-changed curve; open restriction paragraph.

title: Geometry and separable field change of reduced algebraic normalization
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ a reduced scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Define $X^
u$ as the disjoint union of the normalizations [def-sc-normalization] of the finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $X$, with their reduced induced structures, and let $
u:X^
u	o X$ be the canonical map. Then $
u$ is finite and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. The subset $N\subseteq X$ of points whose local rings are integrally closed domains is a dense open, and $
u^{-1}(N)	o N$ is an isomorphism. For every open subscheme $W\subseteq X$, $
u^{-1}(W)	o W$ is canonically the normalization of $W$. If $K/k$ is a separable field extension (every finitely generated subextension is separably generated), the canonical comparison $(X_K)^
u	o X^
u	imes_k K$ is an isomorphism over $X_K=X	imes_k K$ [def-pc-base-change]; no algebraicity or finiteness of $K/k$ is assumed. In particular this comparison is an isomorphism for every extension of an algebraically closed base field $k$.

source.place: Tags 0BXR (lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic), 0C3N (lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields); Morphisms Tags 035Q (lemma-normalization-normal), 035K (lemma-normalization-localization), 0CDV (lemma-normalization-in-terms-of-components). The normal locus equals the isomorphism locus: on an affine chart Spec A with finite integral closure B, it is the complement of the support of the finite A-module B/A.
